newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch says NZ First Maori plan "unaffordable".
newsitem.headline: Birch says NZ First Maori plan "unaffordable".

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch on Wednesday said opposition New Zealand First's policy on Maori land claims was unaffordable.
NZ First launched its policy on Tuesday, proposing the establishment of four new agencies it said would dramatically improve education, training and health standards for Maori.
It said it would also abandon the government's $1 billion fiscal envelope approach to Treaty of Waitangi settlements and extend the time limit for claims to be settled.
Birch said the policy advocated by New Zealand First leader Winston Peters lifted expectations of compensation to levels that were "simply not affordable".
"Would he borrow the money to settle claims or take it from other New Zealanders by cutting health or education or superannuation funding?" Birch said.
New Zealand First joins fellow opposition parties Labour and the Alliance in promising to remove the cap on claims.
Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham said progress in settling claims indicated that fair and affordable settlements were possible.
"To pretend there is a bottomless pit will raise expectations which will later be dashed, leading to greater disillusionment both for Maori and non-Maori," Graham said.
